# Patches to the vendored Ghidra decompiler

Applied on top of Ghidra 12.3 (`918d44e`) by `../vendor.py`, in file-name order, with
`git apply --check` first so that a patch which no longer applies stops the vendoring step
instead of being skipped. The files under `../cpp/` are never edited by hand: a change to
the engine is a new numbered patch here, with a reason in this table and a test that fails
without it.

Each patched file also gets a one-line "Modified for SaturnExplorer" notice in its licence
header, because Apache-2.0 §4(b) asks modified files to say so.

| Patch | Why | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| `0001-cancel-flag.patch` | The bare library has no cancellation hook (Ghidra cancels by killing its decompiler process). Adds a host-owned `std::atomic<bool>*` on `Architecture` and `CancelError` check-points in `FlowInfo::fallthru` (per instruction, so every worklist loop and straight-line run), the jump-table loop of `FlowInfo::generateOps`, `Action::perform` (every action, every level) and `ActionPool::apply` (every 1024 ops); and makes `Funcdata::stageJumpTable` rethrow `CancelError` instead of treating it as a failed jump-table recovery, which swallowed a cancel raised inside the nested "jumptable" simplification. 25 functional lines in 6 files, plus the notices. Cooperative: `Architecture` construction, the body of one action, printing and teardown have no check-point. The spike's `Docs/Decompiler/spike/patches/0001-cancel-flag.patch` plus the `stageJumpTable` rethrow (found in review), the notices, and `CancelError` placed before `RecovError`'s doc comment instead of inside it. | `Sh2DecompilerEngineTests` (`TestCancelDuringJumpTableRecovery`: a cancel requested from inside jump-table simplification must reach the host); `Docs/Decompiler/spike/cancel_spike.cpp`; `DecompilerRunnerTests` from Step 2 |
| `0002-sleigh-reset-null-caches.patch` | `Sleigh::reset` deletes the translator's context and disassembly caches (`clearForDelete`) and then allocates their replacements. If that allocation fails, the deleted pointers stay in the translator, which is a process-global object owned by `SleighArchitecture`'s static map: refusing all later requests (the host's policy after an engine-side out-of-memory) cannot stop its destructor from deleting them again at exit, and the process ended in `free(): double free` (found in the Step 2 review). `clearForDelete` now nulls both pointers after deleting them; `delete` of null is a no-op, so nothing else changes. 2 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` and `DecompilerRunnerTests` reset-OOM children: an allocation in `Sleigh::reset` fails, later requests are refused, and the process must then exit normally through static destruction |
| `0003-translator-ownership-on-init-failure.patch` | `Architecture::restoreFromSpec` held the new translator in a `unique_ptr` until `initialize()` returned. For a `SleighArchitecture` the translator is not the Architecture's: it is the process-global one in `SleighArchitecture`'s static map, reused by every Architecture. An allocation failure in `initialize()` on that reused translator (`reregisterContext`, its new disassembly cache) made the `unique_ptr` delete the map's object (`free(): invalid pointer`, found while testing 0002). The translator is now assigned to `translate` before `initialize()`, so it is owned by each Architecture's existing rules: a plain `Architecture` deletes it, and `SleighArchitecture`'s destructor clears `translate` first. 3 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` reset-OOM child with the failure one allocation later, inside `Sleigh::initialize`: the process must exit normally |
| `0004-funcdata-frees-active-output.patch` | `ActionPrototypeTypes` allocates a `ParamActive` (`Funcdata::initActiveOutput`) that return recovery frees when it completes. `Funcdata::~Funcdata` did not free it, so an analysis abandoned in between -- which the host's cancellation (0001) does, e.g. whenever the SH-2 Pseudocode panel supersedes a request -- leaked one (~48 bytes) per cancel; LeakSanitizer reported it in `DecompilerRunnerTests` whenever the cancel landed there (found in Step 3's review). The destructor now calls `clearActiveOutput()`, which deletes it if present and is a no-op otherwise. 1 functional line in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestFunctionFreesActiveOutput`: creates the state directly, watches its allocation through the test allocator, destroys the Architecture, and requires it freed -- no dependence on where a cancel lands) |
| `0005-sleigh-delay-slot-pc.patch` | PLAN.md A3. A PC-relative load or `mova` in the delay slot of a taken branch reads PC as the branch target + 2, but `disppc2`/`disppc4` computed `inst_start + 4` unconditionally, so the decompiler folded the wrong literal. `bra` and `bsr` -- the delayed branches whose target is in the instruction -- now `globalset` the slot's PC (`slot_tgt`, stored halved, and `slot_pc_valid`) on `inst_next`, and a second `disppc2`/`disppc4` constructor uses it when set. Both context fields are `noflow`, so they hold for the slot's address alone: the instruction after the pair and the one at the target keep their own PC. The engine applies the branch's commits before it parses the slot (`Sleigh::oneInstruction`), and every `Architecture` resets the translator, so no context outlives a request. Conditional (`bt/s`, `bf/s`) and register-target (`jsr`, `jmp`, `braf`, `bsrf`, `rts`) branches are unchanged and stay flagged by the host, as does a `bra`/`bsr` slot that another branch also jumps straight to (the context is per address, so that path would get the slot's PC too). Checked against the SH-1/SH-2 Programming Manual's PC-relative rule and `Sh2DecodeAfterBranch`. A context register (`contextreg`, at register offset 0x400) and 19 functional lines in `superh.sinc`, plus the notice; `sh-2.sla` and `Sh2SpecData.h` regenerated. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestDelaySlotPcRelative`, fixture 3 from `Docs/Decompiler/spike/tools/fixture3.py`): `bra` and `bsr` slots fold the hardware's literal, not the one the old spec read; the load after a `bsr` + slot pair and the load at a `bra` target use their own PC; `bf/s`, `jsr`, `jmp`, `braf`, `rts` and a slot that is also a jump target stay flagged with neither literal folded; `SlaFreshnessTests` |
| `0006-sleigh-sh2-semantics.patch` | Six SH-2 instructions computed wrong results. Their output read as ordinary C, with no warning (found in the review at `6eaa133`). The fixes follow the Renesas SH-1/SH-2 Programming Manual, and Mednafen's SH-2 core (`ss/sh7095_ops.inc`) where the manual leaves a detail open. **`bsr`, `bsrf`, `jsr`:** PR is now written before `delayslot(1)`, so `sts pr` in the slot reads the new return address and `lds ...,pr` in the slot overrides it. **`MAC.L`:** the old cross-product carry test compared `Res2`, which was always 0, so the carry was wrong. It is now one 64-bit accumulate. With S set, it saturates to 48 bits in the direction of the product's sign. **`MAC.W`:** loads are now explicit 2-byte, sign-extended. With S clear, it does a 64-bit accumulate. With S set, it saturates MACL at 32 bits and sets MACH bit 0 on overflow. **`XOR.B #imm,@(R0,GBR)`:** it did an AND; it now does an XOR. **`mov.b/w/l Rm,@-Rn`:** Rm is captured before Rn is decremented, so `mov.l r1,@-r1` stores the old r1. **`DIV1`:** Rm is now read after Rn is shifted, so `div1 r1,r1` uses the shifted value. 42 functional lines added and 121 removed in `superh.sinc` (most of the removals are the old 32-bit MAC.L and MAC.W bodies), plus the notice; `sh-2.sla` and `Sh2SpecData.h` are regenerated. | `Sh2SemanticsTests` runs each instruction on the vendored p-code emulator, using the shipped translator, and compares the result with a reference model transcribed from Mednafen. Coverage: the PR order for all three calls, both ways; MAC.L and MAC.W, 20,000 cases each, S set and clear, including the review's cases and the bytes after a MAC.W operand; XOR.B; all three `@-Rn` sizes with Rn = Rm; DIV1, 5,000 cases each with distinct and aliased registers. Every block fails on the spec before this patch. Also `SlaFreshnessTests`. |
| `0007-cspec-wide-return-order.patch` | `superh.cspec` declared the 8-byte return as `join piece1="r1" piece2="r0"`. In Ghidra `piece1` is the most significant piece, while the big-endian SH ABI returns the high half in R0. So a function returning R0 = 1, R1 = 2 printed `return 0x200000001`, and a caller lent that signature swapped the halves it consumed (found in the review at `8639b80`). The join is now `piece1="r0" piece2="r1"`. 1 functional line, plus the notice; `Sh2SpecData.h` is regenerated. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestPrototypeEligibility`): the callee prints `0x100000002`, and a caller lent its signature stores the shifted high half from R0 and the low half from R1. Also `SlaFreshnessTests`. |
| `0008-cspec-return-address.patch` | `superh.cspec` had no `<returnaddress>`, so the engine could not tell that `jmp @rN` with rN copied from PR is a return. It took it for an unrecovered jump table and printed `(*UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE)(); return;`, and the function's signature was withheld for an unresolved indirect call (found in the review of control-flow recovery at `b488688`). PR is now declared the return address, so such a jump is "treated as return" and its value is the function's return. 3 functional lines, plus the notice; `Sh2SpecData.h` is regenerated. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestFlowUncertainty`: `sts pr,r1; jmp @r1; mov r4,r0` returns its argument and its signature is lent). Also `SlaFreshnessTests`. |
| `0009-keep-unused-loads.patch` | `ActionDeadCode::lastChanceLoad` holds an unused LOAD only when its pointer is already an eventual constant (`isEventualConstant(3,1)`), and `ActionVarnodeProps` drops the hold once heritage moves on. So a load whose address folds only later -- `mov r4,r2; xor r2,r2; add r2,r1; mov.b @r1,r3` with r1 = `SMPC_SF` -- or never (`add r4,r1` first) was removed as dead before the address could be seen to be volatile. A compiler drops an unused load unless it is volatile, so one that remains is there for its effect (found in the review of `20bfde7`). A new `Architecture::keepUnusedLoads`, false by default and set by SaturnExplorer, holds every unused LOAD in `lastChanceLoad` and keeps the hold while it is still a LOAD. Once the pointer is a constant the load becomes a direct varnode read and the existing rules decide: volatile memory keeps it, ordinary memory drops it. A load whose pointer never resolves stays. 4 functional lines in 3 files, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): the late-folding read prints `= SMPC_SF;`, the indexed one `(&SMPC_SF)[param_1]`, and the same late-folding read of work RAM is still removed |
| `0010-load-not-duplicated.patch` | A LOAD is printed once and where it happens. `ActionMarkExplicit` lets a cheap expression with several uses stay implied and prints it at each use, so a read inside it was printed, and appeared to happen, at every use. `ActionMarkImplied` lets a load print where its value is finally used, checking only stores that may alias it and calls, so it could appear after a volatile register write or another read. Found in review:<br>- a poll through a volatile pointer printed a second read after the loop (`aa3f7d1`);<br>- `p[*p].x -= 1` in game code printed the index read twice (`processMultiplier` does not look into a PTRADD's index);<br>- a read before an SMPC command was printed after it, `SMPC_COMREG = param_2; return *param_1;` (`d0ce10a`);<br>- two FIFO reads printed as `*p - *p`, in an order C leaves open (`d0ce10a`);<br>- a read always made printed as `param_2 == 0 && *param_1 == 0`, which C evaluates only when the left side does not decide (`47ae113`).<br><br>A new `Architecture::loadsNotDuplicated`, false by default and set by SaturnExplorer, does two things. `processMultiplier` marks a multi-use expression explicit when any part of it is a LOAD (`containsLoad`). `checkImpliedCover` keeps a LOAD explicit when any other memory operation -- STORE, LOAD, CALLOTHER (volatile reads and writes), CALL, CALLIND -- lies inside the live range of the implied chain it starts, or when that chain enters the right operand of a BOOL_AND or BOOL_OR. A load used once, with nothing in between, still prints inline. About 55 functional lines in 4 files, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): the access ledgers, which check count, width, order and that no two independent reads share a statement, for the volatile-pointer poll, the indexed read-modify-write, the read before a command, the two FIFO reads, two reads through an argument, and reads combined with `&&` and `||` (a genuine branch is the control: its read stays under the branch). `TestGameCode` on a game's work RAM finds no read printed past another access and no statement with two independent reads; with the policy off, 1,656 and 1,283 |
| `0011-ptrsub-char-constant-cast.patch` | `RulePtrsubCharConstant::applyOp` cast the output's type to `TypePointer *` before checking that it is a pointer. UBSan's vptr check reports the cast (found in the review of `47ae113`, through `TestPrototypeEligibility`). The behaviour was right, since the next line checks the metatype and returns. The cast now comes after the check. 3 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` under `-fsanitize=undefined` with vptr |
| `0012-load-in-place.patch` | Two more ways a load left its place, under the same `Architecture::loadsNotDuplicated` policy (found in the review of `5670323`). **For-loop recovery moved a load.** `BlockWhileDo::finalTransform` moves the statement that steps the loop variable, and the one that initialises it, to the end of their blocks so they print in the `for` header; `PcodeOp::isMoveable` let a LOAD cross another LOAD (it already refused stores and user ops). `p = *p; x = *q;` printed `x = *q` in the body and `p = *p` as the step, which C runs after it: the two reads in the other order. A LOAD now cannot cross a LOAD, so such a loop prints as `while` with both reads in place; a step that is already last still prints as a `for`. **A load printed in another block.** An implied expression prints where it is used, which can be a later block: a read before a branch, used on one side only -- `mov.l @r4,r1; tst r5,r5; bt L` -- printed `if (param_2 == 0) { return *param_1; }`, as if read only there. `checkImpliedCover` now keeps a LOAD explicit when any use in its implied chain is in another block than the load. 1 functional line in `coreaction.cc` and 2 in `op.cc`, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): the two for-loop fixtures whose step or initialiser read is not its block's last statement, the fixture whose step is last (still a `for`), and the read before a branch, once in the branch's delay slot. The ledger rejects an access moved within its block (`MovedInBlock`) and a read printed in another block (`conditionalInPrint`); `TestGameCode` counts both: 0 in the game's work RAM, where the second rule hoists 16 reads out of a clause or a call argument |
| `0013-jumptable-loads.patch` | Two jump-table recovery paths that moved or dropped a read, under `loadsNotDuplicated` (found in the review of `0e3cd12`). **A guard folded over a read.** When the block of a switch holds no statement, `JumpBasic::foldInOneGuard` makes the guard branch the switch's default and joins the blocks; `noInterveningStatement` counts stores, calls and NEW as statements but not loads, and an unused load (kept for its effect) has no statement at all. `x = *p; if (x > 3) goto def; y = *q; switch (x)` then printed `y = *q` before the `switch`, as if read for `x > 3` too, also with the read in the jump's delay slot. The fold is now refused when the switch block holds a LOAD other than the table lookup (which stays exempt: 11 game functions fold through one). **A guard on one read bounding a switch on another.** `GuardRecord::valueMatch` took two LOADs from one pointer for one value (upstream's own `TODO: we need to check for aliases`), so `if (*p < 4) switch (*p)` was recovered as a switch on the second read bounded by the first, and the first read and its `if` were dropped; with a store between the reads the guard printed but the switch stayed bounded by the other read. Two different LOAD ops now never match: the guard stays an `if`, both reads stay, and the table, unbounded, is not recovered (the jump is an indirect call and nothing is lent). 16 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): the guarded read, in the block and in the delay slot (both reads stay in separate blocks, the guard an `if`); the control with the table load only (still folded); the second read as the selector (three reads, `if (*param_1 < 4)`, no switch, nothing lent). The ledger rejects both classes: `FoldedIntoSwitch` (two accesses from blocks the flow kept apart by a branch, joined into a switch's block) and the reference run (an access of the flow missing from the output); `TestGameCode` counts both: 0 and 0 |
| `0014-keep-unused-loads-late.patch` | `ActionDeadCode::lastChanceLoad` gives up after the first heritage pass. A load whose only use is a store to a work RAM global that the function overwrites before any read loses that use late: the store becomes a direct write in a later pass and is then removed as overwritten, and the load, unused at a pass where nothing holds it, goes with it. `mov.l @r4,r1; mov.l r1,@global; mov.l #0,@global` printed only `global = 0` (found by the ledger's reference run on game code, in the review of `0e3cd12`: `Ram060a51f6 = *(*(param_1 + 0x18) + 0x28)` and its two reads, gone). Under `keepUnusedLoads` the hold is offered in every pass. One load must not be held: a recovered switch's table lookup, which becomes unused when the switch replaces it; `foldInNormalization` flags it (`PcodeOp::jumptable_lookup`) and the hold and the 0013 fold check skip it. 8 functional lines in 3 files, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): the read stored to an overwritten global stays; the reference run in `TestGameCode` (0 dropped) |
| `0015-proto-param-replace-order.patch` | Two things, found in the review of `0c2dd20`. **A parameter's replacement was allocated after the old one was freed.** `ProtoStoreSymbol::setOutput`, `ProtoStoreInternal::setOutput`, `setInput`, `clearOutput` and `getSymbolBacked` deleted the old parameter and then allocated its replacement; an allocation failure there left the freed pointer in the store, and the store's destructor freed it again at teardown (the host reports an out-of-memory and refuses later requests, but the damaged function is still destroyed). The replacement is now made first; a failed allocation leaves the old parameter in place. **The switch's lookup flag landed on the selector.** `JumpBasic::foldInNormalization` (patch 0014) flagged every LOAD on the model's paths, which reach above the switch variable to the read that produced it: a selector read from memory was flagged as the table lookup, the hold (0014) and the fold check (0013) were off for it, and when every case of the switch went to one destination (`RuleSwitchSingle`) the read went with the switch, its pointer parameter too. Only the loads between the switch variable and the jump are flagged now, walked from the jump's address input to the switch variable through the model's own ops. 17 functional lines in 2 files, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestEngineAllocationFailureInChild`, the `reference` children: an allocation failing as the reference run's actions begin -- the first is this replacement -- must end as Failed with later requests refused, where before the child died in a double free); `TestHardwareVolatility`: a switch whose four cases all return the same value, its selector clamped (recovered by the second-stage model, `JumpBasic2`), keeps `xVar1 = *param_1;` and the pointer parameter |
| `0016-jumpassisted-leak.patch` | `JumpTable::recoverModel` tries an assisted model (`JumpAssisted`) first when the indirect jump's address is a CALLOTHER output, and on failure moved on to the basic model without freeing it: 48 bytes per such jump per analysis (found by LeakSanitizer on the game code's reference runs, in the round after the review of `0c2dd20`). On SH-2 the CALLOTHER is a volatile read: a `jmp @rN` through a pointer kept in memory the user marked volatile, or any such jump in the all-volatile reference run. The failed model is now deleted. 2 functional lines in 1 file, plus the notice. | LeakSanitizer runs of `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`: a jump through a pointer in work RAM, marked and in its reference run) and of the game code: 0 leaks; without the patch the fixture suite reports the 48-byte leak |
| `0017-access-fates.patch` | The engine records how each LOAD and STORE the flow made ends, so that a host can check every memory access is accounted for exactly once (the conservation oracle of the review program's phase 0, replacing the host's heuristics: a pointer read from ordinary memory "may have folded", and the removed blocks parsed from the engine's warning text). `Funcdata` keeps a vector of `AccessRecord { time, pc, addr, store, size, fate }` (`getAccessFates()`), cleared with the function, for the ops the flow made (`flowOps`, the op counter when `followFlow` ends; the loads and stores that rules and actions make, a call's stack parameters, are not the code's). A fate is **`fate_folded_ordinary`**: `RuleLoadVarnode` or `RuleStoreVarnode` made the access a COPY of a Varnode that is not volatile (a volatile one is replaced later by a user op, a real access that stays in the p-code, and is not recorded there); **`fate_unreachable`**: `blockRemoveInternal` of a block removed as unreachable records every access in it first, whether or not a warning is issued, and the silent removal in flow generation comes through it too (destroying an op unsets the inputs of the ops that read its output, so a STORE would no longer know its width); **`fate_switch_lookup`**: a LOAD flagged `jumptable_lookup` (0014, 0015) that `opDestroy` removes; **`fate_dead`**: any other `opDestroy` of a flow access. The destroy-time record is made in `opDestroy` itself, for the LOAD, the STORE, a volatile read or write user op, and the COPY of a volatile Varnode that `replaceVolatile` has not yet replaced, so no path that destroys one (dead code, copy propagation, block removal, the transformations in `double.cc`, `subflow.cc`, `prefersplit.cc`) can lose a record. The jump-table scratch copies of a function have no flow of their own and record nothing. Every opcode change of a flow LOAD or STORE in the fixtures and the game code was checked to come from the two rules above (an instrumented build), so no other path turns one into something else without a record. About 120 functional lines in 5 files, plus the notices. | `Sh2DecompilerTests` (`TestHardwareVolatility`): every reference-run access of every fixture is printed, folded, or removed with said unreachable code, else `ReferenceOk` fails; the records of `storeOverwritten`, `ptrFromRam`, `mailboxFold` and `switchFold` are asserted; `TestGameCode`: 0 dropped over both save states. Mutation: without the `RuleStoreVarnode` hook (or the `RuleLoadVarnode` one) the oracle fails on the fixtures and on the game code; without the block-removal record the mailbox, saved-pointer and literal-switch fixtures fail; with patch 0014 reverted the `ptrFromRam` fixture fails the oracle, which the earlier pointer exemption would have excused |
| `0019-sleigh-sr-rte.patch` | Three SR errors in `superh.sinc`, found by the area 2 oracle (`SaturnExplorerSh2DecodeTests`, ledger A2-1 to A2-3) against Mednafen's SH-2 core (`ss/sh7095_ops.inc`). Their output read as ordinary C, with no warning. **`ldc Rm,SR` and `ldc.l @Rm+,SR`** masked the value with `0x0FFF0FFF`; the CPU keeps T, S, I3-I0, Q and M (`z->SR &= 0x3F3`), so a later `stc sr` read back bits that cannot exist. The mask is now `0x3F3`. **`rte`** masked the stacked SR with `0x63F3`, so SR bits 13 and 14 (the SH-2A's `CS` and `BO`) survived the return; the mask is `0x3F3` too. **`rte` restored SR after its delay slot**; the hardware restores it before (it stores `SR`, then calls `DelayBranch`), so a slot that reads T saw the old one (`rte; movt r2`) and a slot that writes T had the write overwritten (`rte; sett`). `sr = _sr` now comes before `delayslot(1)` and the branch target after it, as patch 0006 did for `bsr`, `bsrf` and `jsr` and PR. 5 functional lines changed, plus the notice; `sh-2.sla` and `Sh2SpecData.h` are regenerated. | `SaturnExplorerSh2DecodeTests`, named shapes and the `ldc`, `ldc.l` and `rte` forms against the Mednafen model: `ldc r0,sr` and `ldc.l @r1+,sr` of `FFFFFFFF` leave `000003F3`; `rte; nop` with stacked `FFFFFFFF` the same; `rte; sett`, `rte; clrt` and `rte; movt r2` see the restored SR (`ldc` control: GBR is not masked). Mutation, each hunk reverted alone and the sla regenerated: the mask on `ldc` fails 2 shapes and 1,267 of 4,000 `ldc`/`ldc.l` cases; the `rte` order fails 3 shapes and 371 of 2,000 `rte` cases; the `rte` mask fails 1 shape and 750 `rte` cases. Also `SlaFreshnessTests` |
| `0020-sleigh-cache-lru.patch` | `Sleigh` keeps its parse trees in `DisassemblyCache`, a ring of 2 (a language whose delay slot is one instruction, `maxdelayslotbytes` = 1, `Sleigh::initialize`) that gives out the oldest entry on a miss, in order of allocation. A hit did not change that order, so a tree hit while it was the oldest was the next one given out. `Sleigh::oneInstruction` looks up an instruction and then its delay slot: with the instruction's tree cached and the slot's not, the slot's lookup took the instruction's own tree, and a delayed branch was built from its slot's parse (`rts` became its slot alone, `bt/s` lost the condition and the jump, no warning). Upstream's own doc comment promises that up to as many distinct addresses as the ring holds get distinct trees; a hit on the oldest broke that. A larger ring does not fix it, only moves the sequence that does (a tree can always be the oldest). A hit now makes the entry the newest, so the cache is least recently used and the promise holds for any size. Reached by the decompiler: `ReturnCheck` (`Sh2Decompiler.cpp`) walks a function's instructions again after the flow, in its own order, so a function that starts with a delayed branch whose slot is also a jump target, with a loop back to the branch, translates the slot, the branch, one plain instruction and the branch again; the branch came out as its slot alone and flowed on past it, and a signature the function is entitled to was withheld (`an indirect jump it does not resolve`). The flow itself (`FlowInfo`) translates each address once, and the engine has no other caller of `oneInstruction`. 8 functional lines in 1 file (`sleigh.cc`), plus the notice. | `SaturnExplorerSh2DecodeTests`: `TestRecycledTreeInDecompiler` (the function above, decompiled: the signature must not be withheld; without the patch it is, with the reason above) and `TestTranslationHistory` (all 5,632 delayed-branch cells: slot, branch, another instruction, branch, the two translations of the branch equal; without the patch all 5,632 differ) |
